app.name: Hashtags

store_name._note: Store name leads with the search keyword in every language (factory rule 10). No platform or company is named anywhere: this app is about hashtags, which belong to nobody, and is not 'for' anyone's product. The in-app name stays the short 'Hashtags'.
store_name.it-IT: Hashtags - Tag per i tuoi Post
store_name.zh-CN: 话题标签 - 帖子标签助手

app.description: Hand-built hashtag sets by topic, copied in one tap, with a counter so you never blow past the 30-tag limit. Build your own sets, search every tag, keep favourites. Works completely offline.
app.target_audience: People who post regularly and retype the same tags every time: small businesses, creators, photographers. They search the store for 'hashtags' and want something that works in five seconds without an account.
app.problem_solved: Choosing hashtags means retyping the same list from a note, or pasting a scraped dump of 30 unrelated words that reads as spam. This gives sets that belong together, a counter that shows where the limit is, and a place to keep the ones that worked.

product_strategy.market_opportunity: A rebuild of the owner's highest-traffic, worst-converting app: 195,198 impressions produced 127 downloads (0.46% CTR) between 2026-03-01 and 2026-08-28, against 4-5% CTR everywhere else in the portfolio. The demand already exists and costs nothing; the listing is what fails. The original also cannot be updated -- its keystore was lost and App Signing was never enabled.
product_strategy.competitive_advantage: Exact search-query match with no trademark in the name, sets written with judgement rather than scraped, a tag counter that addresses the real 30-tag ceiling, everything free, and fully offline.
main_competitors: Generic hashtag-generator apps, most of which are ad walls around a scraped list
Notes apps, which is what most people actually use today
product_strategy.monetization_strategy: Free, supported by Huawei Petal Ads: banner on the topic list and Settings, interstitial only after a set is copied. No ad on the screen where tags are being selected.

technical.dependency_injection: Manual AppContainer (same pattern as the other factory apps)
technical.skeleton: Copy apps/sudoku: it is the cleanest recent app, already has the corrected number-pad-era layout rules, the system-bar fix, the Petal Ads integration and the 9-language string structure. Strip every board, generator and solver file.

features.name: Curated topic sets
features.description: Hashtag sets grouped by topic (travel, food, fitness, photography, art, business, music, nature, fashion, pets, fitness, home, cars, books, gaming, beauty, wedding, sport, coffee, sunset). Each set is a hand-written group of tags that genuinely belong together, shipped inside the app as a JSON asset, never fetched.

features.name: Copy in one tap
features.description: Copy the whole set, or the tags currently selected, to the clipboard as a single space-separated string ready to paste. A confirmation shows what was copied.

features.name: Tag counter and the 30 limit
features.description: A live count of selected tags against the common 30-tag ceiling, with the count turning to the warning colour past it. The limit is presented as a general platform convention, never attributed to a named company.

features.name: Select and deselect individual tags
features.description: Tags are chips; tapping toggles selection. A set opens with everything selected so the common case is one tap, and trimming is optional.

features.name: Custom sets
features.description: Create, rename and delete your own sets; add tags by typing them, with the leading # added automatically and duplicates rejected. Custom sets sit beside the built-in ones.

features.name: Search
features.description: One search box across every tag and every set name, built-in and custom, matching on substring without the # prefix mattering.

features.name: Favourites
features.description: Star any tag; starred tags gather in a Favourites set that behaves like any other and can be copied as a whole.

features.name: Recently copied
features.description: The last ten copies, each restorable to the selection it was made from, because the same combination is usually wanted again.

features.name: Settings
features.description: Theme (light/dark/system), whether a set opens fully selected, privacy information, ads information, about.

features.name: Petal Ads
features.description: Real Huawei Petal Ads SDK: banner on the topic list and Settings; interstitial after a set is copied, under the factory frequency policy. Never on the tag-selection screen.

features.name: Localization
features.description: Interface in all 9 factory languages with RTL support for Arabic. Topic names are translated; the hashtags themselves are not, because tags are a global namespace and translating them would produce tags nobody searches.

features.name: Accessibility
features.description: Content descriptions on every chip and control, 48dp touch targets, font scaling, screen-reader compatible selection state.

screens.name: Topics
screens.purpose: Pick a topic, or reach your own sets.
components: Grid of topic cards, each showing its tag count
Your sets section: custom sets, Favourites, Recently copied

screens.name: Set
components: Tag chips, selectable, starrable on long press
Sticky bar: selected count against 30, Select all / Clear, Copy

screens.name: Edit set
screens.purpose: Create or change a custom set.
components: Tag input that adds # and rejects duplicates

entities.name: Built-in sets
fields: Shipped as a JSON asset, read-only, never written to the database

requirements: Database operations off the main thread.
Copy history capped at 10 rows, oldest evicted.
No user data leaves the device.

content_requirements._note: The tag sets ARE the product. This section is the specification for them, not an afterthought.
requirements: At least 20 topics, each with 25-40 tags.
Tags within a set must plausibly co-occur on a real post: a mix of broad, medium and specific rather than 30 synonyms for the same word.
Lower-case, no spaces, no punctuation beyond the leading #, no numbers unless they are part of an established tag.
No tag that names a company, product or trademark.
No tag associated with engagement-farming schemes (follow-for-follow, like-for-like and their variants): they read as spam and can get a post suppressed.
No claim anywhere -- in the app or the listing -- that any set is trending, best, or guaranteed to increase reach. The app ships no live data and must not imply it does.

monetization.ad_frequency_rules: Banner on Topics (S001) and Settings (S004). Interstitial only after a copy (S002), not in the first 60 seconds after launch, at least 3 minutes apart, at most one per 4 triggers. Never on the tag-selection screen itself. Ad unit IDs come from factory/apps.json via BuildConfig; Huawei test IDs in debug.

requirements: All visible strings in Android string resources; no hard-coded text.
Topic names translated; hashtags never translated -- a translated tag is a tag nobody searches.
Arabic RTL verified; tag chips keep their left-to-right reading because the tags are Latin script.

design.style: Material 3, chips as the primary element, one accent colour used for selection and the counter
requirements: Selected and unselected chips must differ by more than colour alone.
The counter is the most prominent element of the sticky bar.
Touch targets at least 48dp; chips may be visually smaller but must keep the target.
The icon must be designed, not assembled: the original app's 0.46% CTR is the problem being solved, and at the impression stage the icon is most of the product.

privacy._collects_personal_data_note: True because the mandatory Huawei Petal Ads SDK collects OAID, IP, device and app information. The app itself collects nothing about the user.
requirements: Custom sets, favourites and history stay in app-private storage.
android:allowBackup=false.
The only network user is the Petal Ads SDK.
No account, no backend, no analytics, no crash reporting.
No camera, photos, storage, location or notification permission.

appgallery_privacy_tags._note: No data items of its own: the app stores only tags the user typed or starred, which are not personal data. Only the standard Petal Ads block applies, which factory/tools/privacy_tags.py adds automatically and which can now be pushed with `factory.py store <slug> --what privacy-label`.

requirements: No AI claims. The sets are written by hand and shipped as an asset.
Every feature except ads works with no network.
First launch works offline: the built-in sets are an asset, not a download.
Ad failures are silent and leave no empty space.

additional_tests: Unit: the shipped tag asset parses, every topic has 25-40 tags, and no tag repeats within a set.
Unit: no tag in the asset matches the banned-pattern list (trademarks, follow-for-follow variants).
Unit: every tag is lower-case, starts with #, and contains no whitespace.
Unit: tag input normalises (adds #, lower-cases, strips spaces) and rejects duplicates.
Unit: the copy string is space-separated, in selection order, and contains exactly the selected tags.
Unit: the counter reports selection size and flags the 30 boundary at 31, not 30.
Unit: search matches with and without the # prefix, case-insensitively, across built-in and custom sets.
Unit: copy history keeps ten rows and evicts the oldest.
Manual on a real device: copy and paste into another app, RTL, large font, dark mode, airplane mode.

requirements: Same signing keystore as the other factory apps (RELEASE_* secrets).
App Signing MUST be enabled in AppGallery Connect before the first upload (factory rule 11).
versionCode increases every release.
No secrets in git.

distribution_regions: From factory/apps.json defaults.agc.publish_country, pushed with `store --what app-config` before the first submission.
requirements: Real screenshots from the tested build only.
Store copy names no platform and promises no trending data.
Store name leads with the keyword in every language (see app.store_name).
Icon and screenshots uploaded for all 9 languages.

icon.description: A designed icon, not an assembled one: this app's failure was at the impression stage. A bold # as the whole mark, purple on a light ground, legible at 48dp where the original was not.

screenshots.source: Real screenshots from the tested application build
recommended_screens: A set with tags selected and the counter

requirements: No hard-coded ad unit IDs, keys or credentials.
No exported components beyond the launcher activity.
Declare no permission other than INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE.
The tag asset parses once at startup into memory; it is small enough that this is not a loading state.
Search filters without stutter across every tag in the app.
Chip grids recompose per chip, not per screen, when selection changes.
A malformed or missing tag asset is a build failure, caught by a unit test, never a runtime crash.
Clipboard failures show a message rather than failing silently.
Ad failures never block the UI.

acceptance_criteria: Release APK and AAB build with the quality gate passing in --strict mode.
At least 20 topics with 25-40 tags each, and the asset tests pass.
Copying a set puts exactly the selected tags on the clipboard, space-separated, and pasting into another app on a real device produces them.
The counter flags the 30-tag boundary correctly.
A custom set survives an app restart; so do favourites and history.
All strings in all 9 languages; Arabic renders RTL.
Banners appear only on Topics and Settings; the interstitial only after a copy; never on the tag screen.
Airplane mode: every feature works, no empty ad space.
No platform, company or product is named anywhere in the app or the listing.
android:allowBackup is false and no permission beyond INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE is declared.
